pages.text: OreSpawn's monsters shed the best material science in the pack, and it would be rude not to wear it. Two projects in this chapter: a venom-loaded band cut from Emperor Scorpion chitin, and vest plating pressed from Mobzilla's own scales.$(p)Both come off the same shopping list — kill something enormous, keep the pieces.

pages.title: Emperor's Chitin Band
pages.text: An 8% drop from player-killed Emperor Scorpions — the $(l:orespawn_integrations:bestiary/emperor_scorpion)donor$() is house-sized, so bring conviction. Wears in the Artifacts hands slot; Curios and Accessories slots both recognize it.
The patient alternative: six Emperor Scorpion Scales, two gold ingots, one spider eye. Same band, no gambling.

pages.title: The Venom
pages.text: While worn, every melee hit envenoms the target: Poison II for 4 seconds, every single hit, on a 5-second cooldown. Venom particles announce the effect and the tooltip spells it out. Claiming a band earns Venom Wristwear.$(p)Short on scorpions? Desert tombs aren't — cracking the pharaoh's hoard can wake an Emperor Scorpion on the spot. See $(l:orespawn_integrations:living_world/structure_treasures)Structure Treasures$().

pages.title: Mobzilla Plating
pages.text: Four Godzilla Scales, compass points around a Twilight Forest Traveller's Vest. The grid does the riveting.

pages.title: The Plating
pages.text: The plated vest gains +4 Armor and +0.3 knockback resistance, with tooltip lines to prove it; a grindstone strips the plating whenever you want the featherweight back. Rounding up vest and scales earns Wearing the Boss.$(p)$(l:orespawn_integrations:bosses/mobzilla)Mobzilla$() took the hit so you don't have to. Repeatedly. That is the entire theory of armor.
